text:
UCLA Dining provides a range of dining options for students, faculty, staff, and guests. During the academic school year, we offer four all-you-care-to-eat residential restaurants located in Carnesale Commons, Sunset Village, Rieber Court, and De Neve Plaza. Additionally, our quick-service locations include Bruin Cafe, Cafe 1919, The Drey, The Study at Hedrick, Rendezvous, Bruin Bowl and Epicuria at Ackerman, giving you convenient choices across campus.

Each of the four Residential Restaurants serves as many as ten entree options at every meal. All meals are buffet style and all-you-care-to-eat. Pay by Meal Plan, BruinCard Easy Pay, or Meal Ticket only. Cash or credit cards are not accepted at the restaurants.

Bruin Plate
A leader in healthy, sustainable and mindful eating. Located in Sunset Village. Open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner daily during the academic year.

Epicuria at Covel
Simple, delicious Mediterranean meals. Located in Covel Commons. Open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner daily.

Epicuria at Covel
Simple, delicious Mediterranean meals. Located in Covel Commons. Open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner daily.

De Neve Dining
Traditional American dining with a wide variety of options. Located in De Neve Plaza. Offers De Neve Late Night service after regular dinner hours. Open until 2am on weekdays for students with meal plans.

Feast at Rieber
International cuisine and rotating themed meals. Located in Rieber Hall. Open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.

Meal Plan Information
Students living in the residence halls are required to purchase a meal plan. Optional meal plans are available for students living off campus or in university apartments. Meal plans include a set number of swipes per week plus dining dollars for use at quick-service locations. Guests can purchase meal tickets at the door for residential restaurants during breakfast and lunch. Dinner at residential restaurants is restricted to meal plan holders only.

Quick Service Locations
Bruin Cafe: coffee, pastries, grab and go items
The Study at Hedrick: artisan bakery, coffee bar, open 24 hours
Rendezvous: Asian and Latin cuisine
Epicuria at Ackerman: Mediterranean food in the student union
Bruin Bowl: custom bowls, healthy options
The Drey: sandwiches, salads, comfort food

UCLA Dining has been ranked number 1 Best College Food in America by Niche.com for the seventh consecutive year. This is the ninth time in the past ten years that UCLA has claimed the top spot. The rankings are primarily based on student surveys with meal plan affordability also factored in.

UCLA Dining offers a vibrant mix of nearly a dozen quick-service restaurants and all-you-care-to-eat dining halls. Each location is designed with atmosphere, comfort and community in mind.

Bruin Plate emphasizes healthy eating with locally sourced produce and meats, sustainable seafood, organic options, and a wide array of vegetarian and vegan dishes. Communal tables and a private dining room foster connection. Bruin Plate does not serve soda. Instead it offers fruit-infused water such as pineapple, lime, and strawberry. The hall hosts themed food days where all dishes incorporate one ingredient such as garlic day or strawberry day.

Epicuria at Covel and Epicuria at Ackerman are dedicated to Mediterranean menus and flavors. Fresh pasta bar with choice of two sauces, pizza section, and seasonal Mediterranean dishes. Simple cooking methods and fresh ingredients define the menu.

De Neve Dining serves a variety of North, South and Central American food ranging from chili and midwest pepper steak to burgers, fried chicken, pizza and more. There is also a flex bar with salad bar, fruits and vegetarian options. De Neve is known as the traditional dining hall with classic American dishes. De Neve Late Night offers extended hours after dinner service.

The Study at Hedrick blends dining with academics. Students enjoy an artisan bakery, a coffee and tea bar, a 24-hour study space, private meeting rooms, free Wi-Fi, and cozy seating areas.

Rendezvous serves Asian and Latin options including sushi, tacos, and rice bowls.

Bruin Bowl returns this fall with healthy custom-made bowls for guests on the go.

UCLA Dining serves more than 15000 on-campus residents daily. The program sources ingredients from local Southern California farms and works to reduce food waste. Kosher and halal options are available at select locations. Students with food allergies are encouraged to meet with the registered dietician.

At UCLA there are three main dining halls located on the Hill where all of the UCLA dorms and residential living areas are located. Each UCLA dining hall serves different food and has a unique aesthetic.

De Neve
The De Neve dining hall serves a variety of North, South and Central American food, ranging from Cincinnati-style chili and midwest pepper steak to a selection of burgers, fried chicken, pizza and more. There is also a flex bar that includes a salad bar, fruits and vegetarian options. De Neve is known as the traditional UCLA dining hall with classic American dishes and college students cravings. De Neve also serves De Neve Late Night which are extended hours after dinner for the dining hall. Late night runs until around 2am on weekdays and is popular with students studying or coming back from events.

Bruin Plate
Bruin Plate is known as the healthy dining hall that serves seasonal fresh dishes. Some popular items include roasted herb chicken, arugula-topped flatbread, baked potatoes and yams, tuna poke bowls and more. This UCLA dining hall does not serve soda but rather fruit-infused water such as pineapple, lime or strawberry water. Bruin Plate also hosts different food-themed days such as garlic day or strawberry day where all of their dishes incorporate the chosen ingredient. The hall is located slightly uphill from the other dorms which means it is a bit of a walk but most students say it is worth it for the food quality.

Epicuria at Covel
Epicuria at Covel is located on the Hill and serves high quality Mediterranean food. There is a fresh pasta bar with a choice between two sauces as well as a pizza section and more. There are two Epicuria locations at UCLA, one on the Hill and one on campus in Ackerman Union. Epicuria is generally considered one of the nicer dining hall experiences with a more upscale feel compared to De Neve.

Tips from students
Go to Bruin Plate before 6pm if you want to avoid the longest lines. De Neve Late Night is great after a long study session. Epicuria tends to have shorter lines than De Neve at dinner. If you have dietary restrictions Bruin Plate has the most options. The meal plan swipes are only usable at residential restaurants for dinner so plan accordingly if you live off campus.

Post: UCLA dining hall tier list, what do you think?

Comment: Bruin Plate is S tier for me. The food is actually good and healthy and I never feel gross after eating there. The lines are long around 6pm but if you go at like 5:15 or after 7 it's totally fine.

Comment: De Neve is solid for late night. The regular dinner is whatever but late night hits different when you're coming back from the library at midnight. They have decent options until 2am.

Comment: Epicuria is underrated. People sleep on it because it's Mediterranean and sounds boring but the pasta bar is genuinely good. Shorter lines than De Neve most of the time too.

Comment: Hot take but De Neve is the most overrated. The food is fine but nothing special and the lines are always insane at peak hours. I ate there first quarter and switched to Bruin Plate and never looked back.

Comment: For vegetarians Bruin Plate is the obvious choice. Way more options than anywhere else and the quality is actually good. De Neve vegetarian options are kind of sad.

Comment: The themed days at Bruin Plate are so fun. Garlic day is incredible, everything has garlic in it and it somehow works. Strawberry day is also great.

Post: Is the walk to Bruin Plate worth it?

Comment: Yes 100%. Takes like 5 extra minutes from the dorms and the food is so much better. Plus it's less crowded than De Neve.

Comment: Depends where you live. From Rieber it's not bad at all. From De Neve area it's a bit of a hike but still worth it.

Comment: I make the walk every day. Bruin Plate for lunch, sometimes De Neve late night. Best of both worlds.

Comment: The walk is annoying in the rain but otherwise fine. Also a nice break from sitting in your room all day.

Post: Best dining hall for someone who eats a lot?

Comment: De Neve has the most variety. You can literally eat American food, go back for pizza, then get something from the salad bar. It is all you can eat so just go multiple times.

Comment: Feast at Rieber is good for this too. International food rotates a lot so you can try different things.

Comment: Bruin Plate has the best quality per item but if you want sheer volume and variety De Neve is the move.

Post: Is the UCLA meal plan worth it as a second year living off campus?

Comment: Honestly no. If you live off The Hill you can only use it for breakfast and lunch at the residential halls, not dinner unless you have a meal plan swipe. And the off campus meal plan options are limited. I dropped it second year and just cook.

Comment: Depends how much you cook. If you're bad at cooking or don't have time the meal plan is convenient but you're paying a premium for that convenience. The cost per meal works out to like 12-15 dollars which is not great for LA.

Comment: I kept mine second year and regret it. Ended up not using half my swipes and the dining dollars expired. Would not recommend unless you're on the Hill a lot.

Comment: The meal plan makes way more sense if you live in the dorms. You're right there and it's easy to just swipe in. Off campus it's harder to justify.

Post: Breaking down the UCLA meal plan cost - is it worth it?

Post: Breaking down the UCLA meal plan cost - is it worth it?

Comment: Did the math last quarter. Meal plan works out to about 14 dollars per meal if you use every single swipe. You can eat off campus in Westwood for less than that at a lot of places. The only advantage is convenience and not having to think about food.

Comment: For freshmen it's basically required since you live in the dorms. For anyone else it depends on your situation. I think it's worth it if you eat on campus at least twice a day.

Comment: The dining dollars roll over within the year but not between years which is annoying. Make sure you actually use them before the year ends.

Comment: I live in the apartments and kept the optional meal plan. It saves me time during midterms and finals when I don't want to think about groceries. Worth it for me but I understand why people cancel it.

Comment: The late night access at De Neve alone is kind of worth it during finals. Being able to get food at midnight without paying out of pocket is great.

Post: Tips for getting the most out of the meal plan?

Post: Tips for getting the most out of the meal plan?

Comment: Use your dining dollars at The Study at Hedrick for coffee and snacks during the day. Don't waste them on full meals at boutique spots, use swipes for those.

Comment: Go to Bruin Plate for dinner before 5:30 and you avoid the lines. Use late night De Neve for after study sessions. That combination gets you through the day without waiting forever.

Comment: Stack up food from Bruin Plate on days when you have a lot of classes and won't have time to go back. Take fruit, grab a packaged thing. Make your swipes work harder.

UCLA student food review - 5 stars
The dining at UCLA is genuinely impressive for a college campus. Bruin Plate changed how I think about campus food. Everything is fresh, locally sourced, and actually tastes good. The variety across all the dining halls means I never get bored.

UCLA student food review - 4 stars
Food is great overall. Bruin Plate is my favorite, the tuna poke bowl is something I look forward to every week. De Neve is more hit or miss but the late night option saves me during finals. Epicuria is solid if you want something lighter.

UCLA student food review - 5 stars
Coming from a school with bad dining I was shocked at how good UCLA food is. The number 1 ranking is deserved. Bruin Plate alone would put them near the top. Add in the other options and it's hard to complain.

UCLA student food review - 3 stars
Dining is good but gets old after a while. By second quarter you've cycled through everything multiple times. The quality is there but the variety across a whole year is limited. Meal plan also feels expensive if you're not eating every meal there.

UCLA student food review - 4 stars
Vegetarian and vegan options at Bruin Plate are the best I've seen at any university. They actually put thought into plant-based meals instead of just offering a salad bar. Huge plus for me.

UCLA student food review - 5 stars
De Neve Late Night is a lifesaver. Being able to get a real meal at midnight during midterms is something I didn't know I needed until I had it. The food quality at late night is the same as regular hours which is great.

UCLA student food review - 4 stars
Epicuria is slept on. The pasta bar is legitimately good and the Mediterranean options are a nice break from American dining hall food. Lines are usually shorter than De Neve too which is a bonus.

UCLA student food review - 3 stars
The meal plan is a bit pricey especially as an off-campus student. The food quality is there but I wish the cost was lower. Having to pay extra as a non-resident student to access dinner feels unfair.

UCLA student food review - 5 stars
Bruin Plate themed days are so fun. Garlic day is legendary on campus. Everything has garlic and somehow it works. The staff clearly puts effort into making dining a real experience not just fuel.

UCLA student food review - 4 stars
Overall really good dining program. The only consistent complaint I hear is long lines at Bruin Plate and De Neve during peak dinner hours. Go earlier or later and it is much better.

5 stars - Best campus dining hall I have been to
Bruin Plate is genuinely one of the best dining experiences I have had at any university. The food is fresh, healthy, and actually tastes good. They source locally which you can taste in the quality. The tuna poke bowl is incredible and the roasted vegetable options are always well seasoned. No soda here which I appreciate. The fruit water is a nice touch. Lines can be long around 6pm but if you go at 5pm or after 7 it is much more manageable.

4 stars - Great food, annoying lines
The food quality is legitimately great for a dining hall. Bruin Plate lives up to the hype. My only issue is the lines during peak dinner time which can take 20-30 minutes. Go early and it is a completely different experience. The themed days like garlic day are fun and creative. Vegetarian and vegan options are the best on campus by far.

5 stars - My go-to every day
I eat at Bruin Plate almost every day. The menu rotates enough to stay interesting and the quality is consistent. Healthy food that does not taste like health food. The walk from the lower dorms is worth it every single time. Staff is friendly and the dining room is nicer than most dining halls.

3 stars - Good but overrated
Do not get me wrong the food is good. But people talk about it like it is a restaurant and it is still a dining hall. The portions are a bit smaller than De Neve and the healthy options mean less comfort food. If you want a burger or pizza at midnight go to De Neve. If you want to feel good about what you ate go to Bruin Plate.

4 stars - Best option for vegetarians
As a vegetarian Bruin Plate is the only dining hall where I feel like I have real choices. The plant-based options are creative and filling not just a sad salad. The grain bowls and flatbreads are excellent. Highly recommend for anyone with dietary restrictions.

5 stars - Hidden gem timing trick
Go at 5:15pm. No line, full food options, and you can take your time. The people who complain about Bruin Plate lines just go at the wrong time. The food itself is excellent across the board. Arugula flatbread and the roasted herb chicken are my favorites.

4 stars - Great for health conscious students
Really impressed by how seriously they take healthy eating here. Local produce, organic options, no processed junk. The dining hall itself feels cleaner and brighter than De Neve. Only giving 4 stars because it closes earlier which is annoying.

4 stars - Late night is a lifesaver
De Neve Late Night is the best thing about this dining hall. After 10pm when you have been studying for hours and everything else is closed, being able to walk in and get real food is amazing. The late night menu is solid, not just snacks. Runs until about 2am on weeknights which is perfect for finals season.

3 stars - Decent but crowded
The food at De Neve is fine. It is classic American dining hall food, burgers, pizza, fried chicken, chili. Nothing fancy but consistent and filling. The problem is it is always crowded at dinner. Lines regularly hit 20-30 minutes at peak time. If you can handle the crowds the variety is pretty good.

5 stars - Best variety on campus
De Neve has the most options of any dining hall. You can get American comfort food, pizza, salad bar, vegetarian options all in one place. It is all you can eat so you can go back as many times as you want. For people who eat a lot or like variety this is the best spot on The Hill.

4 stars - Go for late night, skip peak dinner
The trick with De Neve is timing. Peak dinner 6-7pm is a nightmare. Go at 5pm or use late night after 10pm and it is a totally different experience. The food quality is consistent and there is always something you want to eat. The flex bar with salad and fruit is always stocked.

2 stars - Too crowded, food is average
I know De Neve is popular but I never understood why. The food is average dining hall food and the lines make it not worth it most of the time. Bruin Plate has better quality and Epicuria is less crowded. De Neve is fine if you need something quick and filling but it is not exciting.

5 stars - Late night during finals
There is no better place on campus during finals week than De Neve Late Night. Open until 2am, real food options, and full of other students also studying. It becomes a social spot as much as a dining hall. The meal plan access at night is a huge perk and one of the best reasons to have a meal plan.

4 stars - Classic and reliable
De Neve is the old reliable of UCLA dining. You always know what you are getting, American comfort food, pizza, salad, desserts. It is not the most exciting but it is always there and always open the latest. The Late Night option makes it essential especially in the second half of the quarter when things get stressful.

5 stars - Most underrated dining hall at UCLA
Nobody talks about Epicuria enough. The pasta bar alone makes it worth visiting. You pick your pasta and sauce and they make it fresh. The pizza is also legitimately good not just campus food good. Mediterranean options like roasted chicken and grain salads are excellent. Lines are almost always shorter than De Neve which is a huge bonus.

4 stars - Great food, nice atmosphere
Epicuria feels a little more upscale than the other dining halls. The Mediterranean focus means lighter, fresher food which is a nice change from the heavy American options at De Neve. The dining room is nicer and less chaotic. My go-to when I want a more relaxed meal.

4 stars - Best pasta on campus
The fresh pasta bar at Epicuria is something special for a college dining hall. You can customize your order and the pasta is actually cooked properly not overdone. The sauces rotate and are well made. If you have not tried Epicuria yet you are missing out.

3 stars - Good but limited variety
The food quality at Epicuria is high but the menu variety is more limited than De Neve. If you are in the mood for Mediterranean it is great. If you want something different you might leave unsatisfied. I rotate between Epicuria and Bruin Plate depending on what I feel like.

5 stars - Go here to avoid De Neve lines
Seriously. If the De Neve line is wrapping around the building just walk to Epicuria. The food is better in my opinion and the wait is maybe 5 minutes. The Mediterranean food is fresh and flavorful and the pasta bar is a highlight. I switched from De Neve to Epicuria as my main dining hall and never looked back.

4 stars - Perfect for a lighter meal
When I want something healthy but not as strict as Bruin Plate, Epicuria is perfect. The Mediterranean dishes are light and satisfying. Fresh ingredients, simple preparation. The olive oil and herb flavors are a nice break from typical dining hall food.

4 stars - Hidden gem dining hall
More people need to know about Epicuria. Consistently good food, shorter lines, nicer space. The pasta bar changes enough that it stays interesting. Would be my top choice if it had the variety of De Neve but for quality and experience it wins.

UCLA Dining Portal

UCLA Dining provides a range of dining options for students, faculty, staff, and guests. During the academic school year we offer four all-you-care-to-eat residential restaurants and multiple quick-service locations.

Residential Restaurants (All-You-Care-To-Eat)
Bruin Plate - Sunset Village - Healthy and sustainable eating, locally sourced ingredients, no soda served, fruit-infused water available, vegetarian and vegan focused
Epicuria at Covel - Covel Commons - Mediterranean cuisine, fresh pasta bar, pizza, simple cooking methods
De Neve Dining - De Neve Plaza - American and international variety, late night service available, flex bar with salad and vegetarian options
Feast at Rieber - Rieber Hall - International rotating menu, themed cuisine nights

Quick Service Locations
Bruin Cafe - Coffee, pastries, grab and go
The Study at Hedrick - Artisan bakery, coffee bar, open 24 hours, study space
Rendezvous - Asian and Latin cuisine
Epicuria at Ackerman - Mediterranean, located in Ackerman Union
Bruin Bowl - Custom bowls, healthy options
The Drey - Sandwiches, comfort food, salads
Cafe 1919 - Coffee and light bites

Meal Plan Information
Residential students are required to purchase a meal plan. Optional plans available for non-residential students. Meal plan dollars can be used at all dining locations. Meal swipes for residential restaurants are available at breakfast and lunch for all meal plan holders. Dinner at residential restaurants is restricted to students living in the residence halls with active meal plans. Guests may purchase meal tickets at the door for breakfast and lunch only. Cash and credit cards not accepted at residential restaurants.

Allergen and Dietary Information
UCLA Dining offers allergen-friendly options at all locations. A registered dietician is available for consultations. Kosher certified options available at select locations. Halal options available. Vegan and vegetarian options clearly labeled at all locations.

Meal Plan Pricing
Prices vary by plan type and are updated each academic year. Contact UCLA Housing for current pricing. Plans range from limited swipe options to unlimited access packages with varying dining dollar amounts included.
